mainTopic: שילוח הקן: the hovering mother, which young count, sending her away again and again or for a מצוה, and lashes for taking the mother
overview: This amud covers three topics in שילוח הקן. First, the גמרא explains why a ברייתא used a hovering mother bird as its example: it teaches that even if her wings touch the nest, one is exempt. To fit this with our משנה, רב יהודה says the ברייתא means wings touching from the side. Next, רבא defends how the משנה reads the פסוק: 'on the fledglings or on the eggs' compares chicks to eggs, and 'nest' teaches that even one counts. A new משנה then teaches that the mother must be sent away even if she returns many times. רבא explains that שַׁלֵּחַ covers repeated sending, and תְּשַׁלַּח teaches that she must be sent away even when wanted for a מצוה, such as a מצורע's purification. After a back-and-forth about why that word is needed, מר בר רב אשי sets the case where the bird was taken intending to send her. Finally, a משנה records רבי יהודה and חכמים arguing over lashes for taking the mother. The גמרא asks for רבי יהודה's reason and brings a proof from the thief and the robber, and רבי זירא begins to question that source on the next amud.

steps.title: Why not teach the case of tree branches instead?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא gave the hovering bird as its example. It could have used a bird sitting on tree branches, and the hovering case would follow even more strongly.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let the ברייתא teach the case of a bird sitting on tree branches, and we would know all the more so that a hovering bird is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions why the ברייתא chose the hovering-bird example to teach the exemption from שילוח הקן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A bird sitting on branches is at least sitting, which looks a bit like sitting on the nest. If even she is exempt, then a hovering bird, which is not sitting at all, is surely exempt. So why didn't the ברייתא teach the stronger, more surprising case?

keyTerms.meaning: Let it teach (why didn't the ברייתא say this instead?)
Branches of a tree where a bird may sit
And all the more so
Hovering (flying over the nest)

phrases.english: Let it teach: tree branches,
phrases.notes: He means a mother bird sitting on branches near the nest instead of on the nest itself.

phrases.english: and all the more so a hovering bird?

steps.triggerLanguage: לִיתְנֵי רוֹבְדֵי אִילָן, וְכׇל שֶׁכֵּן מְעוֹפֶפֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion of the ברייתא about a hovering mother bird.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's choice of the hovering bird as its example
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A teaching should state the less obvious case. Tree branches would teach more, and hovering would follow by קל וחומר.

steps.title: The hovering case teaches that touching wings still exempt
steps.stepSummary: The hovering case was needed to teach that even when her wings touch the nest, one is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: The hovering case was necessary, to teach that even if her wings touch the nest, one is exempt from sending her away.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the hovering case teaches something the branches case could not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With branches, we might think the exemption is only because her wings don't touch the nest. The hovering case adds a new point: even when her wings touch the nest, there is still no obligation.

keyTerms.meaning: It was necessary for him (to teach this)
Her wings are touching the nest
Exempt from the מצוה to send away the mother

phrases.english: The hovering case was necessary for him,
that even if her wings are touching the nest,
one is exempt from sending her away.

steps.triggerLanguage: מְעוֹפֶפֶת אִיצְטְרִיךְ לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that the chosen case carries a new point
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The branches case is the better example, and hovering adds nothing.
steps.terutzMaskana: Hovering teaches that even wings touching the nest do not create an obligation.

steps.title: Our משנה says touching wings do obligate
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges this from our משנה, which says that when her wings touch the nest, one is obligated to send her away.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we learned in our משנה: when her wings touch the nest, one is obligated to send her away!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer it just gave by quoting a משנה that seems to say the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 2 said touching wings still leave one exempt. The משנה says touching wings make one obligated. The two sources seem to contradict each other.

keyTerms.meaning: Obligated to send away the mother

phrases.english: But didn't we learn in a משנה:
when her wings are touching the nest,
one is obligated to send her away!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָאֲנַן תְּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that a hovering bird with wings touching the nest is exempt
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Our משנה explicitly rules the opposite for wings touching the nest.

steps.title: רב יהודה: the ברייתא means touching from the side
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה explains that the exemption applies when her wings touch the nest from the side. The משנה's obligation is when they touch from above.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: when that teaching says she is exempt, it means her wings touch the nest from the side.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה settles the contradiction by showing that the two sources describe different ways of touching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Touching from the side is not like resting on the nest, so one is exempt. Touching from above, as in the משנה, is like sitting on the nest, so one is obligated. Both sources are correct, each in its own case.

keyTerms.meaning: Touching from the side
When it teaches (this ruling)

steps.whatToRemember: A hovering mother bird whose wings touch the nest from the side does not obligate שילוח הקן. If they touch from above, one is obligated.
steps.confusionAlert: Here the word מתניתין refers to the ברייתא that exempts, not to our משנה that obligates. Don't mix them up.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:
When that teaching states its ruling,
phrases.notes: He's talking about the ברייתא that says she is exempt, not our משנה.

phrases.english: it means touching from the side.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה: כִּי קָתָנֵי מַתְנִיתִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 3.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא and the משנה are talking about the same kind of touching.
steps.terutzMaskana: Exempt when touching from the side, obligated when touching from above.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה about one chick or egg
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's words 'if there is only a chick' to start a new discussion.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'If there is only one chick...' and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה. This step only sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה rules that one chick or one egg is enough to obligate, learned from the word 'nest'. It also rules that chicks that can fly or eggs that won't hatch do not obligate, learned from 'on the fledglings or on the eggs'. The next step will question these readings.

keyTerms.meaning: A chick (fledgling)
Etc. (the quote continues in the משנה)

phrases.english: If there is only a chick, etc.
phrases.notes: The full line in the משנה: even one chick or one egg obligates you, because the פסוק says 'nest'.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין שָׁם אֶפְרוֹחַ וְכוּ׳
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even one chick or egg obligates שילוח הקן. Chicks that can fly or eggs that won't hatch do not.

steps.title: A scholar asks רבא: why not read the verses the opposite way?
steps.stepSummary: A scholar suggests swapping the sources. 'Fledglings or eggs' (plural) would require at least two, and 'nest' would include even chicks that fly and eggs that won't hatch.
steps.simpleTranslation: One of the scholars said to רבא: say the opposite. If there is only one chick or one egg, one is exempt, because we need 'fledglings or eggs' in the plural, and that is missing. If there were chicks that can fly or eggs that won't hatch, one is obligated, because it says 'nest', which means any nest.
steps.whatsHappening: A scholar challenges the משנה's reading of the verse and offers a reading that gives the opposite results.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה used 'nest' to include a single chick and used 'fledglings or eggs' to exclude chicks that fly and eggs that won't hatch. The scholar flips it. The plural words could exclude a single one, and 'nest' could include every kind of chick or egg. Nothing obvious decides between the two readings.

keyTerms.meaning: Say the opposite
Chicks that are already able to fly
Eggs that will not hatch
A nest of any kind
And it is not there

phrases.english: One of the scholars said to Rava:
Say the opposite:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין שָׁם אֶפְרוֹחַ אֶלָּא אֶחָד אוֹ בֵּיצָה אַחַת –
phrases.english: if there is only one chick or one egg,
one is exempt from sending,
since we require 'fledglings or eggs,' and that is missing.
phrases.notes: דברים 22:6. Both words are plural, so he thinks you need at least two.

phrases.aramaic: הָיוּ שָׁם אֶפְרוֹחִים מַפְרִיחִים אוֹ בֵּיצִים מוּזָרוֹת,
phrases.english: If there were chicks that can fly or eggs that won't hatch,
one is obligated to send,
as it says 'nest,' meaning a nest of any kind.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ הָהוּא מֵרַבָּנַן לְרָבָא: אֵימָא אִיפְּכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the derivations behind the משנה quoted in step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's way of reading 'nest' and 'fledglings or eggs'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same two phrases could be read the opposite way, which would give opposite rulings.

steps.title: רבא: the long phrase is there to compare chicks to eggs
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that if the Torah only wanted the plural, it could have said 'on them'. Spelling out 'fledglings or eggs' compares the two, so only living chicks and eggs that need their mother count.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, let the verse say 'and the mother is sitting on them'. Why does it say 'on the fledglings or on the eggs'? To compare chicks to eggs and eggs to chicks.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא shows why the scholar's reverse reading does not work and defends the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A short 'on them' would already have been plural. Naming both chicks and eggs must therefore teach a comparison: chicks must be like eggs (still needing the mother), and eggs must be like chicks (able to live). That excludes chicks that fly and eggs that won't hatch, so 'nest' is free to teach that even one is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
Let the verse write
Sitting / resting on
To compare (make a הקש between two things)

steps.whatToRemember: 'On the fledglings or on the eggs' compares the two, so only viable chicks and eggs that still need their mother count. 'Nest' teaches that even a single chick or egg obligates שילוח הקן.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a common method: when the Torah uses extra wording where a shorter word would do, the extra words teach something new. Here they teach a הקש.

phrases.english: If so, let the verse write:
'and the mother is sitting on them.'

phrases.aramaic: מַאי ״וְהָאֵם רֹבֶצֶת עַל הָאֶפְרֹחִים אוֹ עַל הַבֵּיצִים״?
phrases.english: Why does it say 'and the mother is sitting on the fledglings or on the eggs'?
To compare fledglings to eggs
and eggs to fledglings.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם כֵּן, נִכְתּוֹב קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the scholar's challenge in step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the wording is extra and teaches a comparison
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Fledglings or eggs' is just a plural that requires two.
steps.terutzMaskana: The phrase compares chicks to eggs, which excludes chicks that fly and eggs that won't hatch. 'Nest' includes even one.

steps.title: New משנה: Sending the mother away repeatedly, and related cases
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules on three cases. You must send the mother away even if she returns many times. You may not keep the mother and release the young instead. If the young were taken and returned to the nest, there is no new obligation.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you sent the mother away and she came back, even four or five times, you must send her away again, because the פסוק says 'שַׁלֵּחַ תְּשַׁלַּח the mother.' If someone said, 'I'll take the mother and send away the young,' he is still obligated, because the פסוק says to send away the mother. If he took the young, put them back, and then the mother came back onto them, he is exempt from sending her away.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens with three practical rules about sending away the mother bird.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The doubled verb שַׁלֵּחַ תְּשַׁלַּח is used to show that the obligation repeats every time the mother returns. The פסוק names 'the mother' specifically, so releasing the young instead does not count. In the last case the young were already taken into the person's possession, so when they are put back there is no fresh obligation.

keyTerms.meaning: 'You shall surely send away', a doubled verb in the פסוק
Obligated
Exempt
'The children', meaning the chicks or eggs

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
If he sent her away and she came back,
even four or five times, he is obligated,
as it says: 'You shall surely send away the mother.'
If he said: I am taking the mother
and sending away the young, he is obligated,
as it says: 'You shall surely send away the mother.'
If he took the young and returned them to her,
and afterward the mother came back onto them,
he is exempt from sending her away.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ שִׁלְּחָהּ וְחָזְרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the previous discussion of which chicks and eggs count.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: You must send the mother away every time she returns. You cannot substitute the young for the mother. Young that were taken and then returned create no new obligation.
steps.whatToRemember: The source for sending her away again and again is the doubled verb שַׁלֵּחַ תְּשַׁלַּח.

steps.title: Maybe the doubled verb means only twice
steps.stepSummary: A scholar asks רבא why the doubled verb means 'many times'. Maybe שַׁלֵּחַ means once and תְּשַׁלַּח means twice, and that is the limit.
steps.simpleTranslation: One of the scholars said to רבא: But say that שַׁלֵּחַ means one time and תְּשַׁלַּח means two times.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges how the משנה reads the פסוק: two verbs might only mean two times, not four or five.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said you must send the mother away even four or five times. The scholar points out that two words would most naturally give you two sendings. After that, he suggests, the obligation should end.

keyTerms.meaning: 'But say...', proposing a different reading
One time
Two times

phrases.english: GEMARA:
One of the scholars said to Rava:
But say: 'shaleach' means one time,
'teshalach' means two times.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵימָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the משנה's reading of שַׁלֵּחַ תְּשַׁלַּח as meaning unlimited repetition.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's rule that you must send her away even four or five times.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two verbs suggest a limit of two sendings, not an unlimited number.

steps.title: רבא: One word teaches 'a hundred times', the other teaches 'even for a מצוה'
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that שַׁלֵּחַ alone already means as many times as needed. The second word, תְּשַׁלַּח, teaches something else: you must send her away even when you want the bird for a מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: שַׁלֵּחַ means even a hundred times. As for תְּשַׁלַּח: I would only know the rule when you want the bird for a regular, optional purpose. How do I know it applies when you want the bird for a מצוה? The פסוק says תְּשַׁלַּח, meaning in every case.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the challenge by giving each of the two words its own separate teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The scholar assumed both words together count the number of sendings. רבא says no: the single word שַׁלֵּחַ is a general command that applies every time, even a hundred times. The extra word תְּשַׁלַּח is used for a different lesson, that even a bird wanted for a מצוה (such as a מצורע's purification) must be sent away.

keyTerms.meaning: An optional, regular purpose (like eating)
A purpose that fulfills a מצוה
'The verse teaches', introducing a source
In any case

phrases.english: He said to him: 'shaleach' means even a hundred times,
'teshalach': I would only know this for an optional purpose,
phrases.notes: Read it as: from שַׁלֵּחַ alone I'd only know the rule for an optional use. תְּשַׁלַּח comes to add more.

phrases.english: for a מצוה purpose, from where do we know?
The verse says 'teshalach': in every case.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: ״שַׁלֵּחַ״ – אֲפִילּוּ מֵאָה פְּעָמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the scholar's challenge by splitting the two words into two separate teachings.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigns the extra word to a different teaching
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both words together count the sendings, so the limit is two.
steps.terutzMaskana: שַׁלֵּחַ alone means unlimited sendings; תְּשַׁלַּח adds that the rule holds even when the bird is wanted for a מצוה.
steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not saying the doubled verb teaches 'many times'. He says the single word שַׁלֵּחַ already teaches that, which frees תְּשַׁלַּח for a new lesson.

steps.title: Why would a verse be needed for a מצוה case?
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא challenges רבא's teaching. Even without the extra word, a מצוה (an עשה) could never override a rule that is both a לא תעשה and an עשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא, son of רב יוסף בר רבא, said to רב כהנא: So the only reason is that the Torah wrote תְּשַׁלַּח, and without it I would have thought that for a מצוה purpose you don't need to send her away? But this rule is both an עשה and a לא תעשה, and an עשה cannot push aside a לא תעשה together with an עשה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבא's answer: the word תְּשַׁלַּח seems unnecessary, because a basic rule would already give us the same result. The next step answers this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא said we need תְּשַׁלַּח to teach that a bird wanted for a מצוה must still be sent away. רבי אבא says that is obvious. Sending the mother away is both a command (an עשה) and a prohibition (a לא תעשה against taking her), and a מצוה, which is only an עשה, cannot override both together.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The Merciful One', meaning the Torah
'I would have thought', an initial assumption
A positive commandment
A prohibition

keyTerms.term: אֵין עֲשֵׂה דּוֹחֶה לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה וַעֲשֵׂה
keyTerms.meaning: A positive commandment cannot override a prohibition together with a positive commandment

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי אַבָּא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יוֹסֵף בַּר רָבָא לְרַב כָּהֲנָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Abba, son of Rav Yosef bar Rava, said to Rav Kahana:
But is the reason only that the Torah wrote 'teshalach'?
So if not for this,
I would have said that for a מצוה purpose, no?
But it is a positive command and a prohibition,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין עֲשֵׂה דּוֹחֶה לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה וַעֲשֵׂה!
phrases.english: and a positive command does not override a prohibition and a positive command!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא טַעְמָא דִּכְתַב רַחֲמָנָא ״תְּשַׁלַּח״, הָא לָאו הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבא's claim that the word תְּשַׁלַּח is needed for the מצוה case.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's use of תְּשַׁלַּח to teach that the rule applies even for a מצוה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A general rule already says that an עשה cannot override a combined לא תעשה and עשה, so a verse for the מצוה case seems unnecessary.
steps.whyThisMatters: It uses the well-known rule אֵין עֲשֵׂה דּוֹחֶה לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה וַעֲשֵׂה to test whether a derivation from a פסוק is really needed.

steps.title: The extra word is needed for when the mother was already taken
steps.stepSummary: The answer defending רבא: the case is where the person already took the mother. The לאו is broken, so only an עשה remains. One might think another עשה (a מצוה) could override it, so תְּשַׁלַּח teaches that it cannot.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, the word is needed for a case where he broke the rule and took the mother. Since he already broke the לאו, only an עשה is left. You might say: let one עשה (the מצוה he wants the bird for) come and push aside the other עשה (sending her away). So the Torah teaches us that it cannot.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רבי אבא's challenge by pointing to a special case. In that case the extra word really is needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אבא said an עשה can never override a rule that is both a לאו and an עשה. True, but once the person has taken the mother, the לאו is already broken and only the עשה of sending remains. An עשה against an עשה could seem like an even match, so the Torah must tell us the sending still wins.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not needed for that; it is needed for a different case
A negative commandment (a 'do not')
A positive commandment (a 'do')
Let one positive command come and push aside another positive command
It teaches us (that the expected idea is wrong)

steps.confusionAlert: There are two different עשה's here. One is sending away the mother. The other is the outside מצוה the person wants the bird for. The question is whether the second pushes aside the first.

phrases.english: No, it is needed
phrases.notes: He means the extra word תְּשַׁלַּח is needed for the special case that comes next.

phrases.english: where he transgressed and took the mother,
so he has already transgressed the prohibition,
and it is only a positive command that is left,
so let a positive command come and push aside a positive command;
phrases.notes: The first עשה is the מצוה he wants the bird for. The second is the command to send the mother away.

phrases.english: it teaches us [that this is not so].

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא צְרִיכָא, דַּעֲבַר וְשַׁקְלַהּ לְאֵם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי אבא's challenge in step 11 by narrowing רבא's teaching to a specific case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the teaching to a specific case (אוקימתא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Once the לאו is broken and only the עשה remains, another מצוה (an עשה) could override the sending.
steps.terutzMaskana: תְּשַׁלַּח teaches that even then you must send the mother away, even for a מצוה.

steps.title: The answer only works for one view of when the prohibition is broken
steps.stepSummary: The answer fits the view that the לאו is broken as soon as you fail to send right away (קִיְּימוֹ וְלֹא קִיְּימוֹ). But according to the view that it is broken only when you make sending impossible (בִּטְּלוֹ וְלֹא בִּטְּלוֹ), the לאו is not broken until she is slaughtered.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well for the one who teaches 'he fulfilled it or did not fulfill it.' But for the one who teaches 'he ruined it or did not ruin it,' as long as he has not slaughtered her, he has not broken the לאו.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with 'this works for one view' to set up its attack. Then it shows the answer fails according to the other view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a debate about when a person who took the mother counts as breaking the לאו. If it happens right away when he doesn't send her, step 12's case works. If it happens only when he makes sending impossible, for example by slaughtering her, then while she is alive the לאו is still in force. So it is again a לאו plus an עשה, and רבי אבא's question returns.

keyTerms.meaning: This works out well (for one view, which sets up a 'but')
Whether he fulfilled the עשה or did not. If he fails to fulfill it right away, the לאו counts as broken.
Whether he ruined the chance to fulfill the עשה. The לאו counts as broken only once fulfilling it is impossible.

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how a general debate about when a לאו connected to an עשה is broken can decide whether a specific answer about שילוח הקן holds up.

phrases.english: This works well according to the one who teaches
'he fulfilled it or did not fulfill it.'
phrases.notes: This is one side of a debate about when you get lashes for this kind of לאו: if you don't send her right away, the לאו is broken.

phrases.english: But according to the one who teaches
'he ruined it or did not ruin it,'
as long as he has not slaughtered her,
he has not transgressed the prohibition.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנִיחָא לְמַאן דְּתָנֵי קִיְּימוֹ וְלֹא קִיְּימוֹ, אֶלָּא לְמַאן דְּתָנֵי בִּטְּלוֹ וְלֹא בִּטְּלוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 12 that, after taking the mother, only an עשה remains.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: According to בִּטְּלוֹ וְלֹא בִּטְּלוֹ, the לאו is still in force until she is slaughtered. So the case is still a לאו plus an עשה, and the extra word is again unnecessary.

steps.title: According to רבי יהודה, not even the positive command is left
steps.stepSummary: A second challenge: רבי יהודה holds that שַׁלֵּחַ means sending only at the start, before taking. So once the mother was taken, there is no עשה left to send her, and step 12's case makes no sense.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore, according to רבי יהודה, who said that 'שַׁלֵּחַ' means from the start, there isn't even an עשה left!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second, separate problem with the answer from step 12.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 12 depended on the idea that after taking the mother, the עשה to send her still remains. רבי יהודה reads שַׁלֵּחַ as applying only before you take her. So once she is taken, there is no עשה at all to be pushed aside or protected, and the extra word has nothing to teach in that case.

keyTerms.meaning: And furthermore (introduces an additional challenge)
From the start, at the outset
There is not

steps.whatToRemember: The answer that תְּשַׁלַּח covers a case where the mother was already taken now faces two attacks. First, it fails according to בִּטְּלוֹ וְלֹא בִּטְּלוֹ. Second, according to רבי יהודה, no עשה is left at all.

phrases.english: And furthermore, according to Rabbi Yehuda, who said
that 'send away' means at the start,
even a positive command is also not there!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתוּ, לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה דְּאָמַר שַׁלֵּחַ מֵעִיקָּרָא מַשְׁמַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second challenge to the answer in step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption in step 12 that an עשה remains after the mother is taken.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יהודה limits שַׁלֵּחַ to before the taking. So once she is taken, no עשה is left, and step 12's case cannot exist.

steps.title: מר בר רב אשי: He took the bird intending to send her
steps.stepSummary: מר בר רב אשי gives a new case for רבא's teaching. The person took the mother bird intending to send her, so no לאו was broken, and only the עשה of sending remains. One might think another עשה could override it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, מר בר רב אשי said: The case is where he took her intending to send her. There is no לאו here, only an עשה. So one might say: let another עשה come and push aside this עשה.
steps.whatsHappening: After steps 13 and 14 knocked down the earlier answer, מר בר רב אשי gives a new case that explains why the word תְּשַׁלַּח is needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If he took the bird only so that he could send her, he never took her for himself, so the לאו is simply not in play. Only the עשה of sending is left, and an עשה against an עשה could seem like an even match. That is the gap תְּשַׁלַּח closes.

keyTerms.meaning: with the intention of sending her away
there is no לאו (prohibition) here
let one positive מצוה come and push aside another

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אָמַר מָר בַּר רַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rather, Mar bar Rav Ashi said:
For example, where he took her in order to send her away,
where there is no prohibition,
it is only a positive מצוה that is there,
so let a positive מצוה come and push aside a positive מצוה.
phrases.notes: The other מצוה is the one about to be explained: a מצורע who needs birds for his purification.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר מָר בַּר רַב אָשֵׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the case from step 12, which steps 13 and 14 rejected.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since only an עשה is left, another עשה (the מצורע's purification) might override it.
steps.terutzMaskana: תְּשַׁלַּח teaches that even then he must send the bird away.

steps.title: Why would the other מצוה be stronger?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what makes the other עשה stronger than the עשה of sending the bird.
steps.simpleTranslation: What makes this עשה stronger than that עשה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why anyone would think the other עשה could win. This question sets up the explanation that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally two עשה's are equal, so there is no obvious reason for one to push the other aside. If nobody would think that in the first place, a word in the פסוק would not be needed to rule it out.

keyTerms.meaning: what is its strength or advantage?

phrases.english: What is the strength of this positive מצוה
over that positive מצוה?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי אוּלְמֵיהּ דְּהַאי עֲשֵׂה מֵהַאי עֲשֵׂה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the הוה אמינא in step 15.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why one עשה would seem strong enough to override another equal עשה.

steps.title: Peace between husband and wife is very great
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins its answer by recalling how important peace between husband and wife is. The Torah even lets ה' 's name be erased for it in the סוטה water.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have thought so, since the Master said: Great is peace between a man and his wife, for the Torah said that ה' 's name, written in holiness, should be erased in the water.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts to answer by setting up a principle: שלום בית is extremely important. The next step applies this principle to the מצורע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Erasing ה' 's name is normally forbidden, yet the Torah commands it to make peace between a husband and wife. This shows how much weight the Torah gives to שלום בית.

keyTerms.meaning: great is peace
shall be erased in the water (the סוטה ceremony)
it might enter your mind

phrases.english: It would enter your mind, since the Master said:
Great is peace between a man and his wife,
for the Torah said:
The name of the Holy One, Blessed be He,
which is written in holiness,
shall be erased in the water.
phrases.notes: This is about the סוטה, where the written פסוקים with ה' 's name get dissolved in water. במדבר 5:23.

steps.triggerLanguage: סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ, הוֹאִיל וְאָמַר מָר: גָּדוֹל שָׁלוֹם שֶׁבֵּין אִישׁ לְאִשְׁתּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the answer to step 16's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: שלום בית carries enormous weight, which sets up the reason the מצורע's עשה might seem stronger.

steps.title: The מצורע cannot be with his wife until purified
steps.stepSummary: A מצורע is forbidden to his wife until he is purified. So one might think his purification עשה, which needs birds, overrides שילוח הקן. תְּשַׁלַּח teaches that it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this מצורע, as long as he is not purified, is forbidden in marital relations, as it says 'He shall stay outside his tent seven days', and 'his tent' means his wife. You might say that since he is forbidden to his wife, his עשה should push aside the עשה of שילוח הקן. The word teaches us that it does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its answer. The מצורע's purification matters because of שלום בית, so one might think it beats שילוח הקן, but תְּשַׁלַּח teaches otherwise.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra weight comes from the fact that until he is purified, the מצורע is kept apart from his wife. Since peace in the home is so important, his purification could seem urgent enough to override sending the bird. The Torah's extra word says no: he must still send her.

keyTerms.meaning: a person with צרעת, who must be purified using birds
marital relations
'his tent' means his wife
it teaches us (that the הוה אמינא is wrong)

steps.whatToRemember: תְּשַׁלַּח teaches that even when he took the bird intending to send her, and even for a מצורע's purification, he must still send her away.

phrases.english: And this leper,
since as long as he is not purified,
he is forbidden in marital relations,
as it is written: 'And he shall stay outside his tent seven days,'
'his tent' – this is his wife,
from here we learn that he is forbidden in marital relations.
You might have said:
since he is forbidden in marital relations,
let his positive מצוה come
and push aside the positive מצוה of sending away the bird from the nest,
so it teaches us that it does not.
phrases.notes: The teaching comes from the extra word תְּשַׁלַּח in the פסוק.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַאי מְצוֹרָע, כֵּיוָן דְּכַמָּה דְּלָא מִטַּהַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies step 17's principle to the מצורע and completes the answer.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The מצורע's עשה seems stronger because it affects שלום בית, but תְּשַׁלַּח teaches that it still does not override שילוח הקן.

steps.title: משנה: Flogged or sends? רבי יהודה and חכמים argue
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה. For someone who took the mother bird with her young, רבי יהודה says he gets מלקות and does not send her. חכמים say he sends her and gets no מלקות.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: One who takes the mother with the young: רבי יהודה says he is flogged and does not send her away. חכמים say he sends her away and is not flogged.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא's discussion is finished and a new משנה begins with a מחלוקת about what happens after someone took the mother bird.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For חכמים, he can still fix the לאו by sending her afterward, so he gets no מלקות. רבי יהודה gives מלקות, but the משנה does not say why. The גמרא will ask (steps 21-22) whether it is because of a general rule or because of his reading of שַׁלֵּחַ as applying only before the taking.

keyTerms.meaning: משנה, the start of a new משנה
the mother bird together with her young
he receives מלקות (lashes)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think חכמים are being lenient about taking the bird. They hold he still must send her; he just gets no מלקות because sending her fixes the לאו.

phrases.english: MISHNA: One who takes the mother with the young –

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: לוֹקֶה וְאֵינוֹ מְשַׁלֵּחַ,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: He is flogged and does not send her away,
and the Rabbis say:
He sends her away and is not flogged.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ הַנּוֹטֵל אֵם עַל הַבָּנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה; its מחלוקת connects to the view of רבי יהודה mentioned in step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה: מלקות, no sending. חכמים: sending, no מלקות.

steps.title: The rule: a לאו with an עשה to fix it gets no lashes
steps.stepSummary: The משנה gives a general rule: any לאו that comes with a command to get up and do something to fix it does not get מלקות.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is the rule: any לאו that has a 'get up and do' attached to it, we do not give lashes for it.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the general principle behind the view of חכמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the Torah attaches an עשה that repairs the לאו (here, sending the bird away), the punishment is to fix it, not to get lashes. That is why חכמים say he sends her and is not flogged.

keyTerms.meaning: this is the general rule
a לאו that comes with an action to fix it
we do not give lashes

steps.whyThisMatters: This rule, a לאו that can be fixed by an action, applies across all of ש״ס, not only to שילוח הקן.
steps.whatToRemember: חכמים: since the לאו of taking the mother can be fixed by sending her, there are no מלקות. רבי יהודה disagrees in this case and gives מלקות.

phrases.english: This is the principle:
Any prohibition
that has in it a command to arise and do –
we do not give lashes for it.

steps.triggerLanguage: זֶה הַכְּלָל: כׇּל מִצְוַת לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּהּ קוּם עֲשֵׂה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning behind the view of חכמים in step 19.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A לאו that has an attached עשה to fix it does not get מלקות.

steps.title: רבי אבא בר ממל asks for רבי יהודה's reason
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא בר ממל asks whether רבי יהודה gives מלקות because he holds that a לאו שניתק לעשה gets מלקות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא בר ממל asks: Is רבי יהודה's reason that he holds you get lashes even for a prohibition that comes with a command to fix it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens its discussion of the משנה with a question about רבי יהודה's reason. This is the first side of a two-sided question; the second side comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי יהודה gives מלקות for taking the mother bird, and the חכמים do not. The simplest reason would be that רבי יהודה disagrees with the general rule from step 20. In his view, even a לאו that can be fixed by an עשה gets מלקות.

keyTerms.meaning: Asks; raises an open question that needs a solution
A prohibition that is 'moved over' to a positive command, meaning the Torah gives you a מצוה to fix it
One gets lashes (מלקות) for it

phrases.aramaic: גְּמָ׳ בָּעֵי רַבִּי אַבָּא בַּר מֶמֶל:
phrases.english: GEMARA: Rabbi Abba bar Memel asks:
Is the reason of Rabbi Yehuda
because he holds
that for a prohibition linked to a positive command, one gets lashes?

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּעֵי רַבִּי אַבָּא בַּר מֶמֶל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the משנה of steps 19-20 by asking for the reason behind רבי יהודה's view.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבי יהודה's ruling of מלקות comes from a general view that a לאו שניתק לעשה gets מלקות.

steps.title: The second option: שלח applies only at the start
steps.stepSummary: Maybe רבי יהודה agrees there is no מלקות for a לאו שניתק לעשה. Here he gives מלקות only because he reads שלח as a מצוה that applies from the very start.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or maybe, in general, he holds that you do not get lashes for a prohibition that comes with a fixing command. Here the reason is different: he holds that the word 'send' means at the very start.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the second side of the question: maybe רבי יהודה's ruling is special to the case of the bird.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On this reading, רבי יהודה reads the מצוה of שילוח as something you do right when you find the nest, not as a way to fix things after you took the mother. So once you take her, there is nothing left to fix. That means this לאו is not really 'linked to an עשה', and plain מלקות applies.

keyTerms.meaning: Or perhaps; introduces the second side of a question
In general; in other cases
'Send'; the first word of the double phrase שלח תשלח
From the start; at the outset

steps.confusionAlert: Both sides agree that רבי יהודה gives מלקות here. The question is only WHY: a general rule about every לאו שניתק לעשה, or a special reading of the bird פסוק.

phrases.english: Or perhaps, in general, he holds

phrases.aramaic: לָאו שֶׁנִּיתָּק לַעֲשֵׂה אֵין לוֹקִין עָלָיו,
phrases.english: that for a prohibition linked to a positive command, one does not get lashes,
and here, this is the reason:
because he holds
that 'send' means from the very start.
phrases.notes: From דברים 22:7. He means the sending is a מצוה for when you first find the nest, not a way to fix taking her.

steps.triggerLanguage: אוֹ דִלְמָא בְּעָלְמָא סָבַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the two-sided question by offering a second explanation of רבי יהודה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבי יהודה's ruling comes instead from a special reading of שלח, while he keeps the general rule of no מלקות for a לאו שניתק לעשה.

steps.title: Proof from the thief and the robber
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that, according to רבי יהודה, a thief and a robber get מלקות. Robbery is a לאו שניתק לעשה, so the גמרא concludes that רבי יהודה gives מלקות for that kind of לאו in general.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: 'A thief and a robber are included in lashes,' says רבי יהודה. But robbery is a prohibition linked to a positive command, since the Torah says 'Do not rob' and also 'he shall return the stolen item.' So learn from this that רבי יהודה's reason is that he holds you get lashes for such a prohibition.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to answer the question and seems to prove the first side (step 21).
steps.deeperAnalysis: Robbery has a לאו ('do not rob') and also a fixing עשה ('return the stolen item'), so it is a clear לאו שניתק לעשה. Yet רבי יהודה still gives מלקות. So his view seems to be a general rule, not a special reading of the bird פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: A thief who steals secretly
A robber who takes openly, by force
'The Merciful One'; a name for ה' used when quoting the Torah
'And he shall return the stolen item'; the עשה that fixes robbery
Learn from it; the conclusion drawn from a proof

phrases.english: Come and hear:
A thief and a robber
are included among those who get lashes,
these are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.
But here,
it is a prohibition linked to a positive command,
since the Merciful One said 'You shall not rob'
and 'He shall return the stolen item.'
Learn from it
that Rabbi Yehuda's reason is because he holds
that for a prohibition linked to a positive command, one gets lashes.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: גַּנָּב וְגַזְלָן יֶשְׁנָן בִּכְלַל מַלְקוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to settle the two-sided question of steps 21-22 in favor of the first side.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יהודה holds, in general, that a לאו שניתק לעשה gets מלקות.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא in which רבי יהודה gives מלקות to a robber, even though robbery has the fixing מצוה of returning the item.

steps.title: רבי זירא begins to question the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא reminds רבי אבא בר ממל of an earlier warning about ברייתות not taught in a certain study hall. The sentence continues in the next part.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said to him: Didn't I tell you all that any ברייתא that is not taught in the house of...
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא starts pushing back against the proof from the thief and the robber. This line sets up his full point, which finishes in the next part of the daf.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי זירא does not argue with the logic of the proof. Instead he goes after the source: he is about to question whether this ברייתא can be relied on at all. If the ברייתא is not reliable, the proof from step 23 falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: Didn't I tell you all? A reminder of an earlier warning
A taught source; here, a ברייתא

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said to him:
Didn't I tell you all,
that any ברייתא that is not taught in the house of

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי זֵירָא: לָאו אָמֵינָא לְכוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins to reject the proof of step 23 by questioning the reliability of its source.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the ברייתא of the thief and the robber.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא may not be a reliable source. The full reason is completed in the next part of the daf.
